​@souhiyori8640 Singapore: In 1960, the U.S. Central Intelligence Agency (CIA) attempted to bribe Singapore’s founding Prime Minister, Lee Kuan Yew, after a CIA agent was caught trying to recruit a Singaporean intelligence officer from the Special Branch. 

• The Bribe & Counter-Demand: Lee offered to quietly release the agent in exchange for $33 million in U.S. economic-development aid for Singapore. Instead, through an intermediary, the U.S. offered a personal/party payoff of $3.3 million (initially referenced as $3 million or $3.3 million) for Lee and the People's Action Party (PAP), which Lee rejected as an insulting attempt to buy the government.
• The Resolution & Public Exposure: Lee refused the personal money and stood his ground. U.S. Secretary of State Dean Rusk later sent Lee an apology letter in April 1961. When U.S. officials initially denied the plot years later in 1965, Lee publicly exposed the story and produced Rusk’s apology letter as proof, forcing Washington to retract its denial.
